message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Dominated by the most common isotope, ^1H. |
| **Isotopes** | ^1H (protium, 99.98 %), ^2H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ^3H (tritium, trace) | Tritium is radioactive (β‑emitter, half‑life ≈ 12.3 yr). |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron → highly reactive, forms covalent bonds. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements; drives H‑bonding. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | High, reflecting strong attraction between nucleus and lone electron. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative, meaning H⁻ formation is exothermic. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Most stable form under normal conditions. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; requires cryogenic temperatures to liquefy. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Liquid hydrogen exists only at very low temperatures. |
| **Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | About 14.5 % of air’s density. |
| **Density (liquid, 20 K)** | 0.0708 g cm⁻³ | Lower than water; expands upon freezing. |
| **Specific heat (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | High due to two degrees of freedom (rotational). |
| **Heat of vaporization** | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ | Very small; liquid hydrogen evaporates readily. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with O₂, N₂, halogens, metals, acids. | Forms hydrides, acids (e.g., HCl), and many organic compounds. |
| **Bonding** | Forms single covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O, etc.). | Can also form ionic species (H⁺, H⁻). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR | Classic hydrogen atom spectrum. |
| **Magnetic moment** | 2.792847 µ_B (electron spin) | Used in NMR and ESR studies. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant, laboratory reagent, semiconductor doping, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). | Also used in isotope separation and nuclear fusion research. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Atomic number 1, lowest mass, extremely low boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds; essential building block in organic chemistry.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, used in NMR, heavy water), tritium (radioactive, used in fusion and tracer studies).
- **Physical extremes**: Requires cryogenic temperatures to liquefy; expands upon freezing.
- **Energy carrier**: Clean combustion (water) and high specific energy make it a candidate for future fuels.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any particular property or application!
